raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The contiguous-QKV convolution implementation is now on main through #46738. The FlashInfer wrapper can materialize noncontiguous Q/K/V inputs, so numerical graph/eager comparisons alone would not detect a regression that reintroduces the three copies. The graph dispatch also needs coverage for unequal Q/K/V widths, where grouped output is invalid.

## Modifications

- Assert that the real convolution produces contiguous Q/K/V before the FlashInfer graph wrapper can copy them. Continue through the actual wrapper and existing capture/replay output and state comparisons.
- Exercise `kda_extend_in_graph` with unequal Q/K/V widths and check that the original split layout preserves the individual widths and tensor values.

Rebased onto main `180e7a154a46fac3f9381d68b451da1319e29c4f`; current head is `b2b5eb955c540d8c2254bae36665921bb82fc552`. This includes the upstream lint fix in #43902 (a duplicate `tree_cache` keyword in the unrelated decode queue test). The PR patch is byte-for-byte identical to the previously reviewed patch. The remaining diff contains only these two test files; it uses the production implementation from #46738, including its runtime output-plane pitch, and the input-copy helper from #47651.

## Accuracy Tests

The previous head `ae00a8275512adab5163de37c07360df29a8fd9c` was validated on NVIDIA B300/B30Z (SM103), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, CUDA 13.0, Triton 3.8.0 and FlashInfer 0.7.2:

| Registered test file | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/linear/kernels/test_kda_flashinfer_prefill.py` | 4 passed, 0 skipped |
| `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_kda_prefill_graph.py` | 9 passed, 0 skipped; all 5 FlashInfer cases actually executed |
| `test/registered/kernels/ops/mamba/test_causal_conv1d_split_output.py` (existing main regression) | 1 passed, 0 skipped |

The graph suite executes real FlashInfer kernels, CUDA Graph capture/replay with changed inputs, and existing output/state comparisons without changing tolerances. The CPU case isolates graph layout selection and split values. Source hashes were checked before and after testing; a separate FlashInfer 0.7.2 overlay was used with version checks enabled. These are external B300 test results, not a claim that the new upstream CI run is already green.

On current head `b2b5eb955c540d8c2254bae36665921bb82fc552`, repository-configured Ruff checks passed across 7,709 tracked files and Ruff formatting passed across 8,521 tracked files. isort on the changed tests, registered-test lint, Python compilation of the upstream-fixed decode queue test, and `git diff --check` also passed. The complete upstream [Lint workflow](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41398995563) passed on this head on November 2, 2026. The B300 results above belong to the explicitly named previous head; the new rebase did not change this PR's test patch.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A: the remaining changes only add regression coverage. No serving or operator speedup is attributed to this test-only diff.

## Checklist

- [x] Preserve main's production code and avoid a duplicate convolution implementation.
- [x] Keep the regression cases in the existing registered suites.
- [x] Pass isort, repository-selected Ruff checks, Ruff formatting and registered-test lint.
- [x] Validate `ae00a82` on B300, including all FlashInfer graph cases without skips; this test patch is unchanged after the latest baseline update.
- [x] Pass the complete upstream Lint workflow on current head `b2b5eb9`.

files.patch:
@@ -20,6 +20,9 @@
     KDAAttnBackend,
     KDAKernelDispatcher,
 )
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.linear.kda_flashinfer_prefill_graph import (
+    FlashInferKDAPrefillGraph,
+)
 from sglang.srt.layers.attention.linear.kda_prefill_graph import KDAPrefillGraphMetadata
 from sglang.srt.layers.attention.linear.utils import LinearAttnKernelBackend
 from sglang.srt.mem_cache.kv.alloc.id_space import IdSpace
@@ -329,6 +332,19 @@ def test_capacity(self):
 class TestFlashInferKDAPrefillGraph(TestKDAPrefillGraph):
     prefill_backend = LinearAttnKernelBackend.FLASHINFER
 
+    def _capture(self, **kwargs):
+        run = FlashInferKDAPrefillGraph.run
+
+        def check_contiguous_qkv(plan, **inputs):
+            # Check the real convolution output before the wrapper can copy it.
+            # Keep running FlashInfer so replay still checks outputs and states.
+            for name in ("q", "k", "v"):
+                self.assertTrue(inputs[name].is_contiguous(), name)
+            return run(plan, **inputs)
+
+        with patch.object(FlashInferKDAPrefillGraph, "run", check_contiguous_qkv):
+            return super()._capture(**kwargs)
+
     def test_small_buckets_with_padded_sequences(self):
         for num_tokens in (1, 8, 16, 128):
             with self.subTest(num_tokens=num_tokens):

@@ -8,10 +8,12 @@
 """
 
 import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
 from unittest.mock import patch
 
 import torch
 
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.linear import kda_prefill_graph
 from sglang.srt.layers.attention.linear.kda_backend import KDAKernelDispatcher
 from sglang.srt.layers.attention.linear.kernels.kda_flashinfer_prefill import (
     FlashInferKDAPrefillKernel,
@@ -170,6 +172,86 @@ def test_multi_token_batch_stays_on_flashinfer(self):
         self.assertEqual(flashinfer_kernel.calls, 1)
         self.assertEqual(triton_kernel.calls, 0)
 
+    def test_graph_keeps_unequal_qkv_widths_in_split_layout(self):
+        """The graph path must use the legacy split layout for unequal Q/K/V.
+
+        Grouped convolution is only valid when every Q/K/V group has the same
+        width.  ``meta.flashinfer`` selects the graph wrapper, but it must not
+        by itself enable grouped output for models with asymmetric projections.
+        """
+
+        class _RecordingGraph:
+            def __init__(self):
+                self.inputs = None
+
+            def run(self, **kwargs):
+                self.inputs = kwargs
+                return torch.zeros_like(kwargs["v"])
+
+        total_tokens = 3
+        layer = SimpleNamespace(
+            q_dim=2,
+            k_dim=2,
+            v_dim=3,
+            head_q_dim=2,
+            head_k_dim=2,
+            head_v_dim=3,
+            conv_weights=None,
+            bias=None,
+            A_log=torch.zeros(1),
+            dt_bias=torch.zeros(1),
+            lower_bound=-5.0,
+        )
+        graph = _RecordingGraph()
+        meta = SimpleNamespace(
+            track=False,
+            flashinfer=graph,
+            cu_seqlens=torch.tensor([0, total_tokens], dtype=torch.int32),
+            has_initial_state=torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.bool),
+            cache_indices=torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32),
+            conv_block_table=torch.zeros(1, 2, dtype=torch.int32),
+            num_logical_tokens=torch.tensor([total_tokens], dtype=torch.int32),
+            token_index=torch.arange(total_tokens, dtype=torch.int32),
+        )
+        mixed_qkv = torch.arange(total_tokens * 7, dtype=torch.float32).view(
+            total_tokens, 7
+        )
+
+        def convolve(x, *args, output_split_size, **kwargs):
+            self.assertEqual(output_split_size, 0)
+            return x.clone()
+
+        with patch.object(kda_prefill_graph, "causal_conv1d_fn", side_effect=convolve):
+            output = kda_prefill_graph.kda_extend_in_graph(
+                layer=layer,
+                meta=meta,
+                conv_pool=torch.zeros(1, 1, 7),
+                ssm_states=torch.zeros(1, 1, 3, 3),
+                kernel_dispatcher=SimpleNamespace(),
+                mixed_qkv=mixed_qkv,
+                a=torch.zeros(1, total_tokens, 1, 2),
+                b=torch.zeros(1, total_tokens, 1),
+            )
+
+        self.assertEqual(output.shape, (1, total_tokens, 1, 3))
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [
+                tensor.shape[-1]
+                for tensor in (
+                    graph.inputs["q"],
+                    graph.inputs["k"],
+                    graph.inputs["v"],
+                )
+            ],
+            [2, 2, 3],
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            torch.cat([graph.inputs["q"], graph.inputs["k"], graph.inputs["v"]], dim=-1)
+            .squeeze(0)
+            .squeeze(1),
+            mixed_qkv,
+        )
+
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
